weekly.title: The Resurrection
weekly.line: Every Sunday is a little Easter: the day Christ rose from the dead.

psalm.text: This is the day that the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!

reading.text: Why do you seek the living among the dead? He isn't here, but is risen.

midday.text: I am the resurrection and the life.

evening.text: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy.

weekly.intention: Where could you bring new life today: a fresh start, a reconciliation, a word of encouragement?
weekly.ideaLine: Every week can start again. What deserves a fresh start in your life?

weekly.title: The Angels and the Unseen
weekly.line: The week begins by remembering that we live among more than we can see.

psalm.text: Praise the Lord, all you his angels, who are mighty in strength, who fulfil his word.

reading.text: Don't forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.

midday.text: He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

evening.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

weekly.intention: Who is the stranger you could welcome today?
weekly.ideaLine: There is more to the world, and to people, than we can see or measure.

weekly.title: Turning Around
weekly.line: Tuesday remembers John the Baptist, who called people to turn around and start again.

psalm.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

reading.text: Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!

midday.text: In returning and rest you will be saved. In quietness and in confidence will be your strength.

evening.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

weekly.intention: What habit or attitude do you want to turn away from, starting today?
weekly.ideaLine: It's never too late to turn around. What would you like to leave behind?

weekly.title: Keeping Faith
weekly.line: By tradition Judas agreed to betray Jesus on a Wednesday. Today we pray to be faithful.

psalm.text: His compassion doesn't fail. It is new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

reading.text: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.

midday.text: Where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay.

evening.text: Your loving kindness, Lord, is in the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.

weekly.intention: Who is relying on you? Keep one promise to them today, however small.
weekly.ideaLine: Trust is built in small promises kept. Who is relying on you?

weekly.title: Friends at the Table
weekly.line: On a Thursday Jesus shared bread with his friends and washed their feet.

psalm.text: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!

reading.text: No longer do I call you servants. I have called you friends.

midday.text: Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.

evening.text: You prepare a table before me. My cup runs over.

weekly.intention: Who could you share a meal or a real conversation with this week?
weekly.ideaLine: A shared table and a real conversation are among life's deepest goods.

weekly.title: The Cross
weekly.line: Every Friday remembers the day Jesus gave himself for the world.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

midday.text: Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.

evening.text: He was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities; by his wounds we are healed.

weekly.intention: Is there someone you need to forgive, even a little, today?
weekly.ideaLine: The greatest love gives itself away. Where could you give a little more?

weekly.title: Rest and Remembering
weekly.line: Saturday is the Sabbath, the day of rest, when Christians also remember those who have died.

psalm.text: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.

reading.text: Come to me, all you who labour and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

midday.text: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

evening.text: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more.

weekly.intention: Who have you lost? Give thanks for them today, and let yourself rest.
weekly.ideaLine: Stop, rest, and remember the people who made you who you are.

lent.title: Lent: Into the Wilderness
lent.line: For forty days Jesus fasted in the desert. Lent is our forty days.

psalm.text: As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.

reading.text: Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness, and he fasted forty days and forty nights.

midday.text: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God's mouth.

evening.text: Search me, God, and know my heart. Lead me in the everlasting way.

lent.intention: What one thing will you give up or take up this week, to make room for God?
lent.ideaLine: Forty days of less: making room for what matters most.

lent.title: Lent: Prayer
lent.line: The first of the three Lenten disciplines: prayer.

psalm.text: Let my prayer be set before you like incense.

reading.text: When you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret.

midday.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

evening.text: I will lie down in peace and sleep, for you alone, Lord, make me live in safety.

lent.intention: Find five quiet minutes today with no phone, and simply be with God.
lent.ideaLine: In a noisy world, stillness is where we hear what matters.

lent.title: Lent: Fasting and Simplicity
lent.line: The second discipline: fasting, which makes space for what matters.

psalm.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God.

reading.text: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God's mouth.

midday.text: Isn't this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, and to let the oppressed go free?

evening.text: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.

lent.intention: What could you go without today, and give the time or money to someone else?
lent.ideaLine: Going without something reminds you what you really need.

lent.title: Lent: Generosity
lent.line: The third discipline: giving to those in need, quietly.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who considers the poor.

reading.text: When you do merciful deeds, don't let your left hand know what your right hand does.

midday.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

evening.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever.

lent.intention: Give something away today without telling anyone.

lent.title: Lent: Coming Home
lent.line: The story of the prodigal son: however far we wander, the Father runs to meet us.

psalm.text: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness.

reading.text: While he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

midday.text: Return to me, and I will return to you.

evening.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

lent.intention: Is there a relationship you need to come home to? Take one step.
lent.ideaLine: However far you have wandered, the door is open.

lent.title: Lent: The Way of the Cross
lent.line: On Fridays in Lent, Christians walk in their minds the road Jesus walked to the cross.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: He humbled himself, becoming obedient to death, yes, the death of the cross.

midday.text: Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.

evening.text: By his wounds we are healed.

lent.intention: Carry someone else's burden today: a chore, a worry, a hard conversation.

lent.title: Lent: Waiting
lent.line: Lent teaches us to wait, and to trust in the dark.

psalm.text: I wait for the Lord. My soul waits. I hope in his word.

reading.text: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

midday.text: Wait for the Lord. Be strong, and let your heart take courage.

evening.text: Into your hands I commend my spirit.

lent.intention: What are you waiting for in your life? Hand it to God tonight.
lent.ideaLine: Some things can only be waited for. Trust in the dark.

advent.title: Advent: Hope
advent.line: The first week of Advent: in the darkest time of the year, we wait for the light.

psalm.text: I wait for the Lord. My soul waits. I hope in his word.

reading.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.

midday.text: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing.

evening.text: Guide me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation.

advent.intention: Where do you need hope? Bring a little of it to someone else today.
advent.ideaLine: In the darkest time of the year, we wait for the light.

advent.title: Advent: Peace
advent.line: The second week of Advent: waiting for the Prince of Peace.

psalm.text: Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.

reading.text: For to us a child is born. His name shall be called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

midday.text: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you.

evening.text: They shall beat their swords into ploughshares.

advent.intention: Where could you make peace this week: at home, at work, in yourself?
advent.ideaLine: Peace begins small: at home, at work, inside yourself.

advent.title: Advent: Joy
advent.line: The third week of Advent, traditionally called Gaudete: Rejoice!

psalm.text: The Lord has done great things for us, and we are glad.

reading.text: My soul magnifies the Lord. My spirit has rejoiced in God my Saviour.

midday.text: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, Rejoice!

evening.text: The desert shall rejoice and blossom like a rose.

advent.intention: Notice three joys today, and share one of them.
advent.ideaLine: Joy is deeper than happiness. Notice it today.

advent.title: Advent: Love
advent.line: The last week of Advent: Mary says yes, and love comes into the world.

psalm.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever.

reading.text: Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.

midday.text: We love, because he first loved us.

evening.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son.

advent.intention: Who needs to feel loved before Christmas? Tell them.
advent.ideaLine: Who needs to feel loved before the year turns?

christmastide.title: Christmastide: God With Us
christmastide.line: The twelve days of Christmas: God has come to live among us.

psalm.text: Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvellous things!

reading.text: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory.

midday.text: They shall call his name Immanuel, which means, God with us.

evening.text: Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth!

christmastide.intention: Who could use a visit or a call during these twelve days?
christmastide.ideaLine: Twelve days of celebration in the depth of winter.

holyweek.title: Holy Week
holyweek.line: The last week of Jesus' life, as he walks towards the cross.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it.

midday.text: Not my will, but yours, be done.

evening.text: Into your hands I commend my spirit.

holyweek.intention: Stay close to someone who is suffering this week.
holyweek.ideaLine: Facing suffering honestly, and staying close to those who suffer.

ash-wednesday.title: Ash Wednesday
ash-wednesday.line: Lent begins. "Remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return."

psalm.text: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. Create in me a clean heart.

reading.text: Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God; for he is gracious and merciful.

midday.text: For you are dust, and to dust you shall return.

evening.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

ash-wednesday.intention: Choose your Lent: one thing to give up, one thing to take up, one person to give to.
ash-wednesday.ideaLine: A day to face our limits honestly, and begin again.

palm-sunday.title: Palm Sunday
palm-sunday.line: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, and the crowds wave palms.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!

reading.text: Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!

midday.text: Your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey.

evening.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

palm-sunday.intention: Welcome Jesus into the week ahead: what would you like him to find?
palm-sunday.ideaLine: Real authority rides in on a donkey, not a warhorse.

maundy-thursday.title: Maundy Thursday
maundy-thursday.line: The Last Supper, when Jesus washed his friends' feet and gave the new commandment: love one another.

psalm.text: What will I give to the Lord for all his benefits toward me? I will take the cup of salvation.

reading.text: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.

midday.text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another.

evening.text: Not my will, but yours, be done.

maundy-thursday.intention: Do one humble, hidden act of service for someone today.
maundy-thursday.ideaLine: The greatest leader washes his friends' feet.

good-friday.title: Good Friday
good-friday.line: The day Jesus died on the cross. Christians call it good, because of what it won.

psalm.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

reading.text: He was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.

midday.text: It is finished.

evening.text: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!

good-friday.intention: Keep an hour of quiet today, perhaps between noon and three, when Jesus hung on the cross.
good-friday.ideaLine: The day the world remembers the ultimate sacrifice.

holy-saturday.title: Holy Saturday
holy-saturday.line: The day of silence, when Jesus lay in the tomb and the world waited.

psalm.text: I wait for the Lord. My soul waits. I hope in his word.

reading.text: Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and laid it in his own new tomb.

midday.text: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

evening.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep.

holy-saturday.intention: Sit with the silence today. Grief and waiting are part of faith too.
holy-saturday.ideaLine: A day of waiting, when nothing seems to happen.

easter.title: Easter Day
easter.line: Christ is risen! The heart of the Christian faith.

psalm.text: This is the day that the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!

reading.text: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said.

midday.text: Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?

evening.text: I am the resurrection and the life.

easter.intention: Share the joy: send an Easter greeting to someone you haven't spoken to in a while.
easter.ideaLine: The claim at the heart of the West: death is not the end.

ascension.title: Ascension Day
ascension.line: Forty days after Easter, Jesus returns to the Father, promising to be with us always.

psalm.text: God has gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.

reading.text: While they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.

midday.text: I am with you always, even to the end of the age.

evening.text: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses.

ascension.intention: Jesus sent his friends out. Where are you being sent?
ascension.ideaLine: What you have received is meant to be shared.

pentecost.title: Pentecost
pentecost.line: The Holy Spirit comes like wind and fire, and the Church is born.

psalm.text: You send out your Spirit and they are created. You renew the face of the ground.

reading.text: Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and tongues like fire appeared, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit.

midday.text: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control.

evening.text: Come, Holy Spirit.

pentecost.intention: Pick one fruit of the Spirit to practise today: patience, kindness or gentleness.
pentecost.ideaLine: The day a small, frightened group found courage.

trinity.title: Trinity Sunday
trinity.line: One God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, a communion of love.

psalm.text: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty.

reading.text: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptising them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

midday.text: God is love.

evening.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God's love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

trinity.intention: God is a relationship of love. Invest in one of yours today.
trinity.ideaLine: The idea that reality, at its heart, is a relationship of love.

01-01.title: New Year: The Naming of Jesus
01-01.line: A new year, and the day Jesus was named. His name means 'God saves'.

psalm.text: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

reading.text: You shall call his name Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.

midday.text: Behold, I am making all things new.

evening.text: His compassion doesn't fail. It is new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

01-01.intention: Instead of a resolution, choose one way to build something good this year.
01-01.ideaLine: Instead of a resolution, choose one good thing to build.

01-06.title: The Epiphany
01-06.line: The wise men follow a star and find the Christ child: God revealed to the whole world.

psalm.text: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the Lord's glory has risen on you.

reading.text: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy. They offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

midday.text: I am the light of the world.

evening.text: The heavens declare the glory of God.

01-06.intention: The wise men followed a star. What is drawing you towards God?
01-06.ideaLine: What is drawing you towards something greater?

02-02.title: Candlemas
02-02.line: Forty days after Christmas, the baby Jesus is presented in the Temple, and old Simeon sees the light of the world.

psalm.text: The Lord is my light and my salvation.

reading.text: Now you are releasing your servant, Master, in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation, a light for revelation to the nations.

midday.text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn't overcome it.

evening.text: In your light we will see light.

02-02.intention: Light a candle today, and pray for someone who is in a dark place.
02-02.ideaLine: Light a candle for someone in a dark place.

03-17.title: St Patrick
03-17.line: The patron saint of Ireland, once a slave there, who went back to bring the gospel.

psalm.text: The Lord is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer.

reading.text: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me, Christ in me, Christ beneath me, Christ above me.

midday.text: Go and make disciples of all nations.

evening.text: I will both lay myself down in peace and sleep.

03-17.intention: Patrick returned to the people who had enslaved him. Who could you show unexpected grace to?
03-17.ideaLine: A former slave returns to show grace to those who enslaved him.

03-25.title: The Annunciation
03-25.line: The angel Gabriel visits Mary, and she says yes to God.

psalm.text: My soul magnifies the Lord.

reading.text: Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.

midday.text: For nothing spoken by God is impossible.

evening.text: The Word became flesh, and lived among us.

03-25.intention: What is God asking you to say yes to?
03-25.ideaLine: Some of life's greatest turns begin with a simple yes.

06-09.title: St Columba
06-09.line: The Irish monk who founded the monastery on Iona in 563 and brought the gospel to Scotland.

psalm.text: The earth is the Lord's, with its fullness.

reading.text: Go into all the world, and preach the Good News to the whole creation.

midday.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news.

evening.text: The Lord will keep your going out and your coming in.

06-09.intention: Columba made a small island a light to a nation. Where is your 'Iona', the place you could shine?
06-09.ideaLine: How a monastery on Iona became a light to a nation.

06-24.title: The Birth of John the Baptist
06-24.line: The forerunner, who pointed away from himself to Jesus.

psalm.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God.

reading.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

midday.text: Make ready the way of the Lord!

evening.text: You, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High.

06-24.intention: Point attention away from yourself today: praise someone else's work.
06-24.ideaLine: Greatness that steps aside for something greater.

06-29.title: Saints Peter and Paul
06-29.line: The fisherman and the former persecutor: two very different men, both martyrs in Rome.

psalm.text: Their voice has gone out through all the earth.

reading.text: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

midday.text: You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly.

evening.text: My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.

06-29.intention: Peter failed and was restored; Paul was turned around. Who deserves a second chance from you?
06-29.ideaLine: A failed fisherman and a former persecutor changed the world.

07-22.title: St Mary Magdalene
07-22.line: The first witness of the resurrection, called the apostle to the apostles.

psalm.text: My soul thirsts for you, my flesh longs for you.

reading.text: Jesus said to her, "Mary." She turned and said to him, "Rabboni!" which is to say, "Teacher!"

midday.text: I have seen the Lord!

evening.text: Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

07-22.intention: Jesus called her by name. Who could you notice and call by name today?
07-22.ideaLine: Being truly seen and known can change everything.

08-06.title: The Transfiguration
08-06.line: On a mountain, Jesus' friends see him shining with the glory of God.

psalm.text: In your light we will see light.

reading.text: His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.

midday.text: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.

evening.text: The heavens declare the glory of God.

08-06.intention: Look for a moment of glory today: in nature, music or a face.
08-06.ideaLine: Look for a moment of radiance today: in nature, music or a face.

09-29.title: Michaelmas: St Michael and All Angels
09-29.line: The feast of the archangels and the battle of good against evil.

psalm.text: Praise the Lord, all you his angels, who are mighty in strength.

reading.text: There was war in the sky. Michael and his angels made war on the dragon.

midday.text: He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

evening.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

09-29.intention: Stand up for what is good in one small, concrete way today.
09-29.ideaLine: The old feast of the fight between good and evil.

10-02.title: The Guardian Angels
10-02.line: An old tradition says every person, especially every child, is watched over by an angel.

psalm.text: He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

reading.text: See that you don't despise one of these little ones, for in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father.

midday.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

evening.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, Lord, make me live in safety.

10-02.intention: Be a guardian for someone today: look out for a child, a neighbour or a colleague.
10-02.ideaLine: Who looks out for you, and who are you looking out for?

10-04.title: St Francis of Assisi
10-04.line: The rich young man who gave everything away, loved the poor and called the sun his brother.

psalm.text: The earth is the Lord's, with its fullness.

reading.text: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. Even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.

midday.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

evening.text: Let everything that has breath praise the Lord!

10-04.intention: Spend ten minutes outside today, and give thanks for one living thing.
10-04.ideaLine: The rich young man who gave everything away and called the sun his brother.

11-01.title: All Saints
11-01.line: The great company of holy men and women, known and unknown, who have gone before us.

psalm.text: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.

reading.text: Since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us.

midday.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

evening.text: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes.

11-01.intention: Who has shown you what goodness looks like? Thank them, or thank God for them.
11-01.idea: The people who show us goodness
11-01.ideaLine: Who has shown you what a good life looks like?

11-02.title: All Souls
11-02.line: A day to remember and pray for all who have died.

psalm.text: Out of the depths I have cried to you, Lord.

reading.text: In my Father's house are many homes. I am going to prepare a place for you.

midday.text: I am the resurrection and the life.

evening.text: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more.

11-02.intention: Say the names of those you have lost, aloud, and give thanks for them.
11-02.ideaLine: Say the names of those you have lost, and give thanks for them.

11-11.title: Remembrance
11-11.line: We remember those who died in war, and pray for peace.

psalm.text: He makes wars cease to the end of the earth.

reading.text: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

midday.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

evening.text: They shall beat their swords into ploughshares.

11-11.intention: Keep the two minutes' silence at 11:00, and pray for a place at war today.
11-11.ideaLine: We remember those who died in war, and long for peace.

11-16.title: St Margaret of Scotland
11-16.line: The 11th-century queen who fed the poor at her own table and built a ferry for pilgrims.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who considers the poor.

reading.text: I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was a stranger, and you took me in.

midday.text: Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me.

evening.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.

11-16.intention: Feed someone today: buy a coffee, give to a food bank, invite someone in.
11-16.ideaLine: A medieval queen who fed the poor at her own table.

11-30.title: St Andrew
11-30.line: Patron saint of Scotland, the fisherman who brought his brother to Jesus.

psalm.text: Come, see the works of God.

reading.text: He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, "We have found the Messiah!" He brought him to Jesus.

midday.text: Come after me, and I will make you fishers for people.

evening.text: How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace.

11-30.intention: Andrew brought his brother. Who could you invite: to a meal, a conversation, or church?
11-30.ideaLine: Scotland's patron saint, who brought his brother along.

12-06.title: St Nicholas
12-06.line: The 4th-century bishop who gave secret gifts to the poor, the real Santa Claus.

psalm.text: Blessed is he who considers the poor.

reading.text: When you do merciful deeds, don't let your left hand know what your right hand does.

midday.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

evening.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

12-06.intention: Give a secret gift today, and tell your children the real story of St Nicholas.
12-06.ideaLine: The real story behind Santa Claus: gifts given in secret.

12-24.title: Christmas Eve
12-24.line: The holy night: waiting at the manger.

psalm.text: The heavens declare the glory of God.

reading.text: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

midday.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.

evening.text: Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.

12-24.intention: Make room tonight: for God, and for anyone without a place to go.
12-24.ideaLine: Who has no room tonight? Make space for someone.

12-25.title: Christmas Day
12-25.line: God becomes a child. The Word becomes flesh.

psalm.text: Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvellous things!

reading.text: I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people. For there is born to you today a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord.

midday.text: The Word became flesh, and lived among us.

evening.text: Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace.

12-25.intention: Who is alone this Christmas? Reach out to them today.
12-25.ideaLine: The story of light coming into the world, in a stable.

12-26.title: St Stephen
12-26.line: The first Christian martyr, who forgave those who killed him. Good King Wenceslas went out on this day to help the poor.

psalm.text: Into your hands I commend my spirit.

reading.text: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit! Lord, don't hold this sin against them!

midday.text: Love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you.

evening.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

12-26.intention: Like Wenceslas, take something to someone in need today.
12-26.ideaLine: Forgiving your enemies, and taking something to someone in need.

easterweek.title: Easter Week: Christ Is Risen
easterweek.line: The week after Easter is one long celebration: the tomb is empty and everything has changed.

psalm.text: This is the day that the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!

reading.text: Jesus himself came near, and went with them. Their eyes were opened, and they recognised him.

midday.text: Peace be to you.

evening.text: Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.

easterweek.intention: The risen Jesus walked with two sad friends. Walk alongside someone who is struggling today.
easterweek.ideaLine: After the darkest day, something unexpected begins.

0.title: The Resurrection
0.line: Every Sunday is a little Easter: the day Christ rose from the dead.
0.ideaLine: Some happiness fades by Monday. What kind of joy could last through a hard week?

psalm.text: Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

reading.text: Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.

midday.text: Don't be grieved, for the joy of the Lord is your strength.

evening.text: You have put gladness in my heart, more than when their grain and their new wine are increased.

0.intention: What gave you a deep, quiet gladness this week, rather than a quick thrill? Make room for more of it today.

0.title: The Resurrection
0.line: Every Sunday is a little Easter: the day Christ rose from the dead.
0.ideaLine: Darkness rarely has the last word. Where have you seen light come back?

psalm.text: Light dawns in the darkness for the upright, gracious, merciful, and righteous.

reading.text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn't overcome it.

midday.text: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the Lord's glory has risen on you.

evening.text: Even the darkness doesn't hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you.

0.intention: Think of a dark time that eased. Thank someone who helped bring the light back.

0.title: The Resurrection
0.line: Every Sunday is a little Easter: the day Christ rose from the dead.
0.ideaLine: Great things often start tiny. What small beginning in your life deserves a little hope?

psalm.text: He who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will certainly come again with joy, carrying his sheaves.

reading.text: The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took, and sowed in his field, which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree.

midday.text: Indeed, who despises the day of small things?

evening.text: He won't break a bruised reed. He won't quench a dimly burning wick.

0.intention: Plant something small today: a seed, a habit, a kind word. Then leave it to grow.

0.title: The Resurrection
0.line: Every Sunday is a little Easter, kept in memory of the morning Christ rose from the dead.
0.ideaLine: When did you last see something the way a child does, as if for the first time?

psalm.text: Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.

reading.text: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God's Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.

midday.text: From the lips of babes and infants you have established strength.

evening.text: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.

0.intention: Ask a child, or the child you were, one honest question about the world today, and take the answer seriously.

1.title: The Angels and the Unseen
1.line: Monday keeps the old devotion to the angels: a reminder that we live among more than we can see.
1.ideaLine: Most of what matters goes unnoticed. What would you see if you slowed down and really looked?

psalm.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

reading.text: Moses said, “I will go now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burned.”

midday.text: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don't toil, neither do they spin.

evening.text: I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches.

1.intention: Choose one ordinary thing today, a tree, a face, a cup of tea, and give it two full minutes of your attention.

1.title: The Angels and the Unseen
1.line: Monday keeps the old devotion to the angels: a reminder that we live among more than we can see.
1.ideaLine: Every stranger is someone's whole world. What might you see in the next one you meet?

psalm.text: The Lord preserves the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and widow.

reading.text: The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt.

midday.text: I was a stranger and you took me in.

evening.text: For I am a stranger with you, a foreigner, as all my fathers were.

1.intention: Learn the name of someone you see often but have never spoken to.

1.title: The Angels and the Unseen
1.line: Monday keeps the old devotion to the angels: a reminder that we live among more than we can see.
1.ideaLine: The night sky has made people wonder for as long as there have been people. When did you last look up?

psalm.text: The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork.

reading.text: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made.

midday.text: He counts the number of the stars. He calls them all by their names.

evening.text: When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have ordained, what is man, that you think of him?

1.intention: Step outside tonight for five minutes and look at the sky. What does it make you feel?

1.title: The Angels and the Unseen
1.line: Monday remembers the angels, and that the world holds more than we can see.
1.ideaLine: What beautiful thing have you walked past this week without noticing?

psalm.text: One thing I have asked of the Lord, that I will seek after: that I may dwell in the Lord's house all the days of my life, to see the Lord's beauty.

reading.text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts.

midday.text: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don't toil, neither do they spin, yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.

evening.text: Honour and majesty are before him. Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

1.intention: Find one beautiful thing today, a face, a building, a few bars of music, and stay with it for two full minutes.

2.title: Turning Around
2.line: Tuesday keeps the old call to repentance: to turn round, face the truth and begin again.
2.ideaLine: Two small words that can mend a great deal. Is there an apology you have been putting off?

psalm.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

reading.text: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.”

midday.text: Leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

evening.text: I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn't hide my iniquity.

2.intention: Say sorry to one person today, plainly, without a ‘but’.

2.title: Turning Around
2.line: Tuesday keeps the old call to repentance: to turn round, face the truth and begin again.
2.ideaLine: The hardest person to be truthful with is often yourself. What do you already know but avoid looking at?

psalm.text: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.

reading.text: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but don't consider the beam that is in your own eye?

midday.text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us.

evening.text: Who can discern his errors? Forgive me from hidden errors.

2.intention: Before bed, write down one thing you did today that you are not proud of, and one you are.

2.title: Turning Around
2.line: Tuesday keeps the old call to repentance: to turn round, face the truth and begin again.
2.ideaLine: Sorry is the start. Is there something you could put right, not just regret?

psalm.text: Depart from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it.

reading.text: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”

midday.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the Lord require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

evening.text: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.

2.intention: Think of a wrong you have done. Take one practical step today to repair it: return, repay, or rebuild.

2.title: Turning Around
2.line: Tuesday recalls John the Baptist, who called people to turn round and begin again.
2.ideaLine: Where in your life is a small lie doing more harm than the truth would?

psalm.text: Behold, you desire truth in the inward parts. You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.

reading.text: Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbour, for we are members of one another.

midday.text: Lord, who shall dwell in your sanctuary? … He who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart.

evening.text: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.

2.intention: Today, say one true thing you have been avoiding, kindly and plainly.

2.title: Turning Around
2.line: Tuesday recalls John the Baptist, who called people to turn round and begin again.
2.ideaLine: Is there an anger you have been feeding that it is time to set down?

psalm.text: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath. Don't fret; it leads only to evildoing.

reading.text: Be angry, and don't sin. Don't let the sun go down on your wrath.

midday.text: Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.

evening.text: Stand in awe, and don't sin. Search your own heart on your bed, and be still.

2.intention: The next time you feel anger rising today, wait ten breaths before you speak or type.

2.title: Turning Around
2.line: Tuesday recalls John the Baptist, who called people to turn round and begin again.
2.ideaLine: When did you last change your mind, and what made it possible?

psalm.text: He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.

reading.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the Lord require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

midday.text: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.

evening.text: Lord, my heart isn't arrogant, nor my eyes lofty; nor do I concern myself with great matters, or things too wonderful for me.

2.intention: Ask someone you trust where they think you might be wrong, and listen to the answer without defending yourself.

3.title: Keeping Faith
3.line: Wednesday remembers God's faithfulness, and asks for the grace to stay faithful in return.
3.ideaLine: Anyone can start. What helps a person keep going when the shine has worn off?

psalm.text: I waited patiently for the Lord. He turned to me, and heard my cry.

reading.text: We also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance; and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope.

midday.text: Let's not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don't give up.

evening.text: Rest in the Lord, and wait patiently for him.

3.intention: What good thing are you tempted to give up on? Do one small piece of it today.

3.title: Keeping Faith
3.line: Wednesday remembers God's faithfulness, and asks for the grace to stay faithful in return.
3.ideaLine: Loyalty shows when things go wrong. Who has stood by you, and who needs you to stand by them?

psalm.text: Your loving kindness, Lord, is in the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.

reading.text: Where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.

midday.text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.

evening.text: I will sing of the loving kindness of the Lord forever. With my mouth, I will make known your faithfulness to all generations.

3.intention: Get in touch with someone going through a hard patch, and let them know you are still there.

3.title: Keeping Faith
3.line: Wednesday remembers God's faithfulness, and asks for the grace to stay faithful in return.
3.ideaLine: Trust is easy when all is clear. What helps you hold on when you cannot see the way ahead?

psalm.text: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God.

reading.text: But those who wait for the Lord will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.

midday.text: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.

evening.text: My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.

3.intention: Name one worry you cannot fix today. Write it down, and for now, let it rest there.

3.title: Keeping Faith
3.line: Wednesday is for faithfulness: God's to us, and ours to God and to each other.
3.ideaLine: What would change if you did today's ordinary work as if it mattered?

psalm.text: Let the favour of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us.

reading.text: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.

midday.text: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might.

evening.text: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

3.intention: Pick one dull task today and do it carefully and well, as a gift to whoever it serves. Then stop on time.

3.title: Keeping Faith
3.line: Wednesday is for faithfulness: God's to us, and ours to God and to each other.
3.ideaLine: What do you hope to be like when you are old, and are you becoming it?

psalm.text: Yes, even when I am old and grey-haired, God, don't forsake me, until I have declared your strength to the next generation.

reading.text: Even to old age I am he, and even to grey hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.

midday.text: They will still produce fruit in old age. They will be full of sap and green.

evening.text: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

3.intention: Call or visit someone older than you today, and ask them what they have learned that they wish they had known sooner.

3.title: Keeping Faith
3.line: Wednesday is for faithfulness: God's to us, and ours to God and to each other.
3.ideaLine: If someone read your bank statement, what would they say you love?

psalm.text: If riches increase, don't set your heart on them.

reading.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

midday.text: For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can't carry anything out.

evening.text: Better is a little that the righteous has, than the abundance of many wicked.

3.intention: Look at what you spent last week. Choose one thing to give up this week, and give that money to someone who needs it.

4.title: Friends at the Table
4.line: Thursday remembers the Last Supper, when Jesus ate with his friends on the night before he died.
4.ideaLine: A welcome costs little and can change a life. Who could you make room for?

psalm.text: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.

reading.text: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind; and you will be blessed, because they don't have the resources to repay you.

midday.text: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.

evening.text: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.

4.intention: Invite someone who rarely gets asked: for coffee, a meal, or just a proper conversation.

4.title: Friends at the Table
4.line: Thursday remembers the Last Supper, when Jesus ate with his friends on the night before he died.
4.ideaLine: Something happens when people eat together. When did a shared meal last change your day?

psalm.text: Wine that makes the heart of man glad, oil to make his face to shine, and bread that strengthens man's heart.

reading.text: Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart.

midday.text: Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart.

evening.text: When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them. Their eyes were opened and they recognized him.

4.intention: Eat one meal today with someone else, phones away, and pause to be thankful before you begin.

4.title: Friends at the Table
4.line: Thursday remembers the Last Supper, when Jesus ate with his friends on the night before he died.
4.ideaLine: Everyone needs a place where they are missed when they are not there. Where is yours?

psalm.text: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity.

reading.text: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.

midday.text: God sets the lonely in families.

evening.text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow.

4.intention: Turn up for something local today or this week: a club, a choir, a service, a neighbour's door.

4.title: Friends at the Table
4.line: Thursday remembers the Last Supper, the meal Jesus shared with his friends the night before he died.
4.ideaLine: Do you have a friend who tells you the truth, and are you that friend to anyone?

psalm.text: Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness; let him reprove me, it is like oil on the head; don't let my head refuse it.

reading.text: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

midday.text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.

evening.text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend's countenance.

4.intention: Thank a friend who once told you something hard that you needed to hear.

5.title: The Cross
5.line: Every Friday remembers the day Jesus died on the cross, and the love that held nothing back.
5.ideaLine: Nobody gets through life alone. Whose load could you help carry today?

psalm.text: Cast your burden on the Lord and he will sustain you.

reading.text: Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

midday.text: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering.

evening.text: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, even the God who is our salvation.

5.intention: Ask someone who is struggling what would actually help, and then do it.

5.title: The Cross
5.line: Every Friday remembers the day Jesus died on the cross, and the love that held nothing back.
5.ideaLine: A grudge is heavy to carry. What would it take to set one down?

psalm.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

reading.text: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.”

midday.text: Bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.

evening.text: But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared.

5.intention: Name one grudge you are holding. Today, wish that person well, even if you cannot yet say it to them.

5.title: The Cross
5.line: Every Friday remembers the day Jesus died on the cross, and the love that held nothing back.
5.ideaLine: Pain is part of every life. What do you need when it is your turn to hurt?

psalm.text: The Lord is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

reading.text: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair; pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed.

midday.text: Jesus wept.

evening.text: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.

5.intention: Be gentle with your own hurt today, and sit for a while with someone else in theirs without trying to fix it.

5.title: The Cross
5.line: Every Friday remembers the day Jesus died on the cross, and the love that held nothing back.
5.ideaLine: What would you do today if you were a little less afraid?

psalm.text: The Lord is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear?

reading.text: Haven't I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don't be afraid. Don't be dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.

midday.text: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the Lord.

evening.text: In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.

5.intention: Do one right thing today that costs you something: speak up for someone, or own a mistake in front of others.

6.title: Rest and Remembering
6.line: Saturday is the day of rest and the quiet day after the cross, when the dead are remembered with hope.
6.ideaLine: We are told we always need more. What would it feel like to have enough?

psalm.text: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.

reading.text: Not that I speak because of lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.

midday.text: Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me.

evening.text: Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.

6.intention: Go a whole day without buying anything you don't need, and notice what you already have.

6.title: Rest and Remembering
6.line: Saturday is the day of rest and the quiet day after the cross, when the dead are remembered with hope.
6.ideaLine: We stand on the shoulders of people we never met. Who carried something good down to you?

psalm.text: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

reading.text: Therefore let's also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let's run with perseverance the race that is set before us.

midday.text: One generation will commend your works to another, and will declare your mighty acts.

evening.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, Lord, make me live in safety.

6.intention: Remember someone who has died and shaped you. Tell someone else a story about them.

6.title: Rest and Remembering
6.line: Saturday is the day of rest and the quiet day after the cross, when the dead are remembered with hope.
6.ideaLine: Gratitude changes how a day feels. What have you been given that you have not yet thanked anyone for?

psalm.text: Praise the Lord, my soul, and don't forget all his benefits.

reading.text: In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.

midday.text: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice. He fell on his face at Jesus' feet, giving him thanks.

evening.text: It is a good thing to give thanks to the Lord, to sing praises to your name, Most High, to proclaim your loving kindness in the morning, and your faithfulness every night.

6.intention: Write down three things from this week you are grateful for, and thank one person in writing.

6.title: Rest and Remembering
6.line: Saturday is the old day of rest, and the day Christ lay in the tomb: a day to stop, give thanks and remember.
6.ideaLine: What would it be like to let go of tomorrow's worries for one afternoon?

psalm.text: How many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.

reading.text: See the birds of the sky, that they don't sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren't you of much more value than they?

midday.text: The birds of the sky nest by them. They sing among the branches.

evening.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, Lord, make me live in safety.

6.intention: Spend twenty minutes outside today with no task. Watch one bird, tree or patch of sky until you really see it.

6.title: Rest and Remembering
6.line: Saturday is the old day of rest, and the day Christ lay in the tomb: a day to stop, give thanks and remember.
6.ideaLine: What would you notice about your own life if you stopped measuring it against other people's?

psalm.text: The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.

reading.text: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have.

midday.text: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.

evening.text: Return to your rest, my soul, for the Lord has dealt bountifully with you.

6.intention: Each time you catch yourself envying someone today, name one good thing in your own life instead. Tonight, write three of them down.
